query: What concrete linkage and privacy-preserving protocol will we use to connect survey/experiment responses to behavioral transactions while preserving anonymity and IRB requirements?

response.query: What concrete linkage and privacy-preserving protocol will we use to connect survey/experiment responses to behavioral transactions while preserving anonymity and IRB requirements?
response.answer: We will use a cryptographic hash linkage protocol to connect responses to transactions, ensuring anonymity and compliance with IRB requirements. Each response and transaction will be linked via unique, irreversible hash values. This method preserves privacy and confidentiality.

results.content: All reports and complaints of alleged sexual harassment will be evaluated by the Director of the Office of Employment Equity (the Title IX Coordinator for Employees) to determine whether the alleged conduct falls within the scope of the Title IX Policy. If not, the Director will determine whether the alleged conduct, if true, would constitute prohibited sexual harassment under this Policy, and, if so, proceed in accordance with the Discrimination, Harassment, Workplace Violence, and Retaliation Complaint Process: Complaints Against University Employees and Third Parties (“Complaint Process”).[3] 248 III. REPORTING DISCRIMINATION AND HARASSMENT Any member of the University community alleging discrimination or harassment on the basis of membership in any of the protected classes is encouraged to report it immediately to the Office of Employment Equity.[4] University supervisors and managers are required to inform the Office of Employment Equity of any reported conduct prohibited by this Policy involving other employees.
